body.statement: Suppose \(\widetilde D\) is diagonal and strictly positive and \(\widetilde A\Sigma+\Sigma\widetilde A^{\top}=\widetilde D\). With \(\lambda=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), the common rescaling \(A=\widetilde A/\lambda\) and \(D=\widetilde D/\lambda\) preserves \(\Sigma\), satisfies \(A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}=D\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), and preserves \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\). It is the unique representative of the positive common-scaling class with trace-one diffusion.
body.justification: The lemma separates an observationally irrelevant common time-unit choice from the substantive edge-margin and norm restrictions.
body.gap: The trace-one restriction is a gauge choice for this bounded-fiber analysis, not a modeling condition attributed to the one-edge sign-identification literature.
body.consumer: Every sector, threshold, contact, and inference result can be interpreted for an arbitrary strictly positive diagonal diffusion after converting \(\eta\) and \(M\) to the normalized time unit.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(\widetilde D\) is diagonal and strictly positive, \(\lambda=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)>0\).  Dividing the assumed Lyapunov equation by \(\lambda\) gives
\[
 (\widetilde A/\lambda)\Sigma+\Sigma(\widetilde A/\lambda)^{\top}
 =\widetilde D/\lambda.
\]
Thus the displayed \(A\) and \(D\) preserve \(\Sigma\), and
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(D)=\lambda^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)=1.
\]
Moreover \(A_{12}A_{21}=\lambda^{-2}\widetilde A_{12}\widetilde A_{21}\); since \(\lambda^{-2}>0\), its sign is unchanged.  A positive common rescaling has the form \((c\widetilde A,c\widetilde D)\), and its diffusion trace is \(c\lambda\).  The equation \(c\lambda=1\) has the unique solution \(c=\lambda^{-1}\).  This proves uniqueness of the trace-one representative.  In particular, raw edge and norm bounds transform as \(|A_{ij}|=|\widetilde A_{ij}|/\lambda\) and \(\lVert A\rVert_F=\lVert\widetilde A\rVert_F/\lambda\), which explains why \(\eta\) and \(M\) are stated in the selected time unit.
